title: Stocks rally broadly after the US midterm elections
summary: US stocks rose sharply on Wednesday, with Microsoft and Amazon each up about 6% and the Nasdaq leading. Several market reports tie the move to relief now that the election result is known, though sources disagree on the exact index numbers.
why: Markets do not like surprises. When a big unknown gets settled, investors often buy. But rallies fueled by relief can fade fast, so one good day does not tell you what comes next.

title: AMD reports third quarter sales above its guide
summary: AMD said its quarterly revenue was $13.4 billion, with data center sales up 97% from a year ago. It also said growth should speed up next quarter as new AI chips ramp up.
why: AMD sells chips that power AI. Fast growth in that business is why people pay a high price for the stock (its P/E is about 105). A high price means the company has to keep delivering, or the stock can drop.

title: The Treasury announces how much it plans to borrow
summary: The US Treasury published its borrowing plan on Wednesday. The amount of government borrowing can affect how much interest the government has to offer on its bonds.
why: If the government sells more bonds, it may have to pay higher interest to attract buyers. Higher bond rates can make stocks look less attractive by comparison.

title: Vertiv reports big sales growth, then falls sharply a week later
summary: Vertiv reported third quarter sales up 61%, and its stock jumped on the news. On November 4 it fell almost 13% in a single day, and we could not confirm why.
why: A company can do very well and its stock can still fall if investors expected even more, or if they decide to take profits. Always check the price, not just the headline.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October
summary: The monthly average yield on the 10 year US Treasury bond rose to 5.13% in October, from 4.99% in September and 4.06% a year earlier.
why: A bond is a loan to the government. When it pays more interest, safer choices become more attractive, which can put pressure on expensive stocks.
